generated_examples.rule: Each source becomes one research-only example. No parcel BNG applicability, gain-plan approval, nutrient mitigation, protected-site conclusion, ecological licence or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Recheck planning permission, biodiversity gain condition, gain-plan approval, gain-site registration/allocation, legal agreement, nutrient certificate and HRA/licensing states as distinct legal/process gates.

third_pass_examples.rule: Recheck application dates, 6 August 2026 exemptions, 2 November 2026 NSIP commencement, calculator versions, provisional-certificate expiry, dataset freshness and superseding ecological evidence.

fourth_pass_examples.rule: Recheck national/dataset/map evidence against exact red-line geometry, habitat survey, conservation objectives, feature condition, catchment, metric inputs and secured mitigation. Geographic overlap alone is never promoted.

extra_examples.fact: The new 0.2-hectare-or-below exemption applies from 6 August 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not apply the future exemption to an earlier planning application; exact application date and red-line area are required.

extra_examples.fact: De minimis and small-site exemptions have priority-habitat caveats.
extra_examples.gate: Approximate low habitat impact is not enough; priority habitat and exact impacted area/linear habitat must be checked.

extra_examples.fact: BNG becomes mandatory for relevant NSIP DCO applications from 2 November 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat the rule as already applicable to an earlier DCO application.

extra_examples.ref: Planning permission versus Biodiversity Gain Plan approval
extra_examples.fact: BNG is generally discharged through a post-permission Biodiversity Gain Plan.
extra_examples.gate: Planning permission alone does not discharge the biodiversity gain condition or permit commencement where that condition applies.

extra_examples.fact: The register can show accepted sites and allocations to developments.
extra_examples.gate: A registered gain site does not prove unallocated units remain available for a new development.

extra_examples.fact: Off-site units can be formally allocated to a development.
extra_examples.gate: Recorded allocation is not the LPA's approval of the Biodiversity Gain Plan.

extra_examples.fact: An HMMP explains habitat management and monitoring but does not replace the legal agreement.
extra_examples.gate: Do not score a draft or agreed HMMP as legal security where legal security is required.

extra_examples.fact: Significant on-site and off-site gains can be legally secured for at least 30 years.
extra_examples.gate: A 30-year legal term does not prove the habitat has already reached its target condition.

extra_examples.fact: Statutory credits are a last-resort BNG route after on-site and off-site options.
extra_examples.gate: Do not assume credits are available/acceptable merely because a project has a biodiversity-unit shortfall.

extra_examples.ref: Credit price table versus project cost
extra_examples.fact: Defra publishes habitat-specific statutory credit prices and reviews them periodically.
extra_examples.gate: Published prices are not the final project cost until exact metric shortfall, habitat category and credit quantity are established.

extra_examples.fact: The 2025/26 statutory-credit report records national income and habitat procurement.
extra_examples.gate: National market totals do not demonstrate a target project's credit requirement or approval probability.

extra_examples.fact: Habitat creation required under another scheme may count fully, partly or not at all toward BNG depending on the rule.
extra_examples.gate: Do not double-count mitigation or other scheme habitat automatically as additional BNG.

extra_examples.fact: The statutory metric converts habitat survey inputs into biodiversity units.
extra_examples.gate: Incorrect habitat type, condition, area or strategic-significance inputs can invalidate the result; exact ecological evidence is required.

extra_examples.ref: Metric tool version versus site facts
extra_examples.fact: Defra maintains official metric tools and version history.
extra_examples.gate: Using an official tool version does not validate the user's underlying habitat survey or geometry.

extra_examples.fact: Nutrient calculators quantify nutrient budgets for relevant development in specified catchments.
extra_examples.gate: A zero or mitigated budget is evidence input, not the competent authority's final Habitats Regulations conclusion.

extra_examples.fact: The River Eden calculator was updated in March 2026 for revised catchment boundaries.
extra_examples.gate: Older catchment assumptions must not override the current calculator boundary and treatment-work logic.

extra_examples.fact: The River Camel calculator was updated in March 2026 for revised catchment boundaries.
extra_examples.gate: A previous nutrient-budget output should be recalculated if it relied on the superseded catchment boundary.

extra_examples.ref: Future WINEP upgrade versus present mitigation
extra_examples.fact: The calculator incorporates future wastewater-treatment improvements under WINEP.
extra_examples.gate: Future treatment upgrades are calculation assumptions and must not be described as infrastructure already delivered today.

extra_examples.fact: A provisional Nutrient Credit Certificate can expire if planning-permission milestones are not met and Natural England not informed within the defined period.
extra_examples.gate: Expired provisional credits must not be treated as still reserved.

extra_examples.fact: Material development or nutrient-budget changes must be notified and can require certificate amendment/recalculation.
extra_examples.gate: A certificate tied to an earlier scheme quantum cannot automatically be reused after material design or assumption changes.

extra_examples.ref: Poole credit application versus planning permission
extra_examples.fact: A planning application reference is needed to apply for Natural England credits, but permission need not yet have been granted.
extra_examples.gate: Credit-application eligibility is not evidence that planning permission exists.

extra_examples.fact: The Natural England scheme offers nutrient mitigation credits for eligible development.
extra_examples.gate: Purchased/reserved credits support mitigation but do not replace the competent authority's HRA and planning decision.

extra_examples.fact: The Planning Data SSSI layer includes some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
extra_examples.gate: Confirm exact Natural England designation and site features before using a polygon intersection in parcel scoring.

extra_examples.fact: Natural England assigns condition categories to designated SSSI features.
extra_examples.gate: Favourable or unfavourable condition does not itself determine whether a development's impacts are acceptable.

extra_examples.fact: The SAC dataset collector is current but the newest underlying data found is older and provenance is mixed.
extra_examples.gate: Use current conservation objectives/designation evidence for HRA rather than relying solely on the national planning-data copy.

extra_examples.fact: SPA mapping identifies protected bird-site geography.
extra_examples.gate: Intersection/proximity is a screening trigger and not a likely-significant-effect or integrity conclusion.

extra_examples.fact: Ramsar mapping identifies internationally protected wetland sites.
extra_examples.gate: Mapped proximity does not replace protected-site conservation objectives, pathway analysis and HRA evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Planning authorities must investigate proposals on or potentially affecting protected sites and consult/assess as required.
extra_examples.gate: Distance alone is not a sufficient impact test; pathways, scale, construction and operational effects matter.

extra_examples.fact: Official standing advice warns smaller ancient woodlands may be absent from inventories and records can change.
extra_examples.gate: No inventory hit must not be converted into 'no ancient woodland'; field and historic evidence can still identify it.

extra_examples.fact: Ancient woodland and ancient/veteran trees are irreplaceable habitats and compensation is a last resort.
extra_examples.gate: Proposed compensation cannot be used to erase the initial loss/deterioration assessment or wholly-exceptional-reasons test.

extra_examples.ref: LNRS area versus metric strategic significance
extra_examples.fact: Defra publishes LNRS areas and responsible authorities across England.
extra_examples.gate: Being inside an LNRS geography does not automatically create high strategic significance; the adopted/current local strategy and mapped measure are required.

extra_examples.fact: From 6 August 2026 qualifying small developments can consider on-site and off-site options together.
extra_examples.gate: Do not apply the changed hierarchy to earlier applications or to development that does not meet the small-development criteria.

extra_examples.fact: Official guidance expects habitat creation/enhancement to start within the specified timeframe where work has not started by allocation.
extra_examples.gate: Allocated units do not prove habitat works have started or ecological outcomes have been achieved.

extra_examples.ref: Credit proof of purchase versus gain-plan approval
extra_examples.fact: Proof of statutory-credit purchase is evidence submitted with the Biodiversity Gain Plan.
extra_examples.gate: Proof of purchase is one plan input and does not itself approve the plan or discharge the biodiversity gain condition.

extra_examples.fact: A Biodiversity Gain Plan affecting irreplaceable habitat requires specific compensation information.
extra_examples.gate: Standard biodiversity-unit uplift cannot substitute for the separate treatment of irreplaceable habitat impacts.

extra_examples.fact: BNG calculations depend on the habitats and geometry within the development red line plus any relevant off-site gains.
extra_examples.gate: Do not promote from regional habitat/dataset evidence without exact canonical parcel geometry, current habitat survey and reconciled metric inputs.
